subject: FastPay pilot: concurrency matrix, streaming SLA targets & ratecard
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Fisk <jordan.fisk@fastpay.com>, Infra Team <infra@fastpay.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-27T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: FastPay pilot: concurrency matrix, streaming SLA targets & ratecard

Jordan — thanks again for the productive call earlier. Below is a concise recap and the proposal we'd like you to review before the engineering sync next week. I pulled in Aditya and Marissa to confirm technical assumptions and pricing.

Recap (what we heard)
- FastPay needs a low-latency streaming inference path for payment routing suggestions (p95 target ~300-350ms).
- Expected peak: 800 QPS sustained during business hours; burst to 2000 QPS for short windows (20–60s) around batch settlements.
- Concurrency model preference: long-lived websocket connections from FastPay edge, multiplexed to handle multiple parallel prompt requests per connection.
- Pilot scope: validate streaming stability and end-to-end latency with representative payloads and KV-cache warmup.

Redwood proposal (high level)
- Connection pool: provision initial allowance of 250 persistent connections for pilot (can increase to 500 for the full pilot test).
- Per-connection parallelism: allow up to 4 simultaneous inference streams per websocket (application-level multiplexing), giving an effective pilot concurrency of 250*4 = 1000 parallel in-flight requests.
- Aggregate target: sustain 800 QPS with ability to absorb bursts to 2000 QPS for up to 30s using burst credits and autoscaling buffers.
- Latency SLO: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 350ms for streaming chunk delivery (100ms chunk cadence), extra headroom for >1s long-form outputs.
- Rate limits & throttles: default per-account QPS cap remains 1000; for the pilot we can temporarily raise to 2000 with a burst window.
- Pilot commercial: 30-day technical pilot with $5k platform credit, waived setup fees. If pilot validates targets, propose a 12-month reserved capacity contract with a 20% consumption discount and connection credits.

Attachments: I attached a compact ratecard and a connection matrix spreadsheet with the configuration we recommend. Please review the rows labeled "Pilot" and "Prod target" in the spreadsheet.

Next steps (action items)
1) FastPay: confirm representative payloads and the times for a 2-hr load window we can use for a soak test (Jordan).
2) Redwood: schedule a technical kickoff + shared load-test plan (Aditya).
3) Commercial: we'll prepare a pilot agreement and DocuSign link once FastPay confirms scope (Marissa).

Please reply with any immediate concerns or if you'd prefer different starting concurrency numbers. Happy to adjust — objective is to get a small, fast pilot running.

Cheers,

Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions (North America)
Redwood Inference
+1 415 555 0192
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Attachment: fastpay-conn-matrix.xlsx (pilot/prod rows)

Subject: Re: FastPay pilot: concurrency matrix, streaming SLA targets & ratecard

Thanks Ben — appreciate the clear write-up. A few quick clarifications from our side before we lock the dates: 

- The 800 QPS sustained aligns with our expectations; we'll confirm the exact payload sizes (likely 2–4 KB per request).
- For the websocket strategy: we plan to terminate TLS at the edge and maintain 200 persistent connections per region (we operate primarily in us-east and us-west). Is the pilot quota per-region or global?
- Burst behavior: 30s max bursts are common during settlement. If Redwood can guarantee burst smoothing with the suggested credits, that should be fine.

Action items on our side:
- I'll send sample payloads and the preferred 2-hour soak windows by Monday EOD.
- We're ok with the pilot credit offer; can you confirm the expected observability (token-level latency traces, per-connection metrics) we'll get during the pilot?

I'll loop in our SRE (infra@fastpay.com) to coordinate the load test.

Best,
Jordan Fisk
Head of Integrations
FastPay
jordan.fisk@fastpay.com

Jordan / FastPay infra — quick technical notes from our runtime/serving side to make sure we're aligned before the load window: 

1) Quotas & geographic scope- Our pilot quotas are provisioned per-account but we can carve region-specific allowances. Proposal: start pilot in us-east only (200 connections), then expand to us-west for the second soak. This reduces cold-cache variance during the first test.

2) Connection multiplexing & parallelism- We support application-level multiplexing (4 streams/connection) and adaptive batching at the router. In practice, for 4 KB payloads the steady-state per-token compute is dominated by model decode; multiplexing helps keep latency stable by smoothing arrival bursts.

3) Burst handling and autoscaling- For the 30s bursts, we'll enable short-lived autoscaling buffers: we maintain an ephemeral standby pool that can be consumed by the pilot (subject to burst credits). We'll instrument a sliding window (30s) that allows temporary QPS up to 2500 with progressive throttling if the burst persists >90s.

4) Observability- During the pilot you'll get: token-level latency traces, per-connection p50/p95, KV-cache hit rates, and per-model CPU/GPU utilization dashboards. We'll share a Grafana invite and a pre-built dashboard.

5) Test checklist (pre-kickoff)
- FastPay: send representative payloads and expected concurrency mix (ratio of short calls vs long-form).
- Redwood: provide a canonical load-test harness and a signed-in Grafana/trace link.

If you're comfortable with the pilot starting in us-east, we'll provision the connection allowance and send over a provisional DocuSign with the pilot terms (Marissa will own commercial).

— Aditya
